nodes.name: Phases as turns
nodes.definition: A complex number of size one is a turn e^{iθ}; multiplying two of them adds their angles.

nodes.name: The Bloch sphere
nodes.definition: Every pure qubit state is a point on a sphere, fixed by two angles.

nodes.name: Pauli matrices
nodes.definition: X flips 0 and 1, Z flips the sign of 1, Y does both; each squares to the identity.

nodes.name: Commutators and anticommutators
nodes.definition: AB − BA and AB + BA measure whether order matters; two different Pauli matrices anticommute.

nodes.name: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
nodes.definition: Directions a matrix only stretches, and the stretch factors.

nodes.name: Unitary operators
nodes.definition: Maps that keep every length; quantum gates and time evolution are unitary.

nodes.name: Commuting observables share eigenvectors
nodes.definition: If two Hermitian matrices commute they can be measured together: they have a common eigenbasis.

nodes.name: Projective measurement and the Born rule
nodes.definition: Measuring an observable leaves the state in one eigenspace, with chance equal to the squared overlap.

nodes.name: The qubit
nodes.definition: A two-level quantum system: the unit of quantum information.

nodes.name: One-qubit gates
nodes.definition: H, S, T and the rotations R_z(θ) turn the Bloch sphere; T is a π/4 turn about z up to a phase.

nodes.name: Registers
nodes.definition: n qubits together need 2ⁿ amplitudes, the reason quantum states are hard to store classically.

nodes.name: CNOT
nodes.definition: Flips the target qubit when the control is 1; the basic two-qubit gate.

nodes.name: Circuit diagrams
nodes.definition: Wires are qubits, time runs to the right, boxes are gates and meters.

nodes.name: Reading a register
nodes.definition: Measuring some or all qubits in the 0/1 basis, possibly in the middle of a circuit.

nodes.name: Phase kickback
nodes.definition: A controlled gate whose control starts in |+⟩ writes the target's eigenvalue onto the control's phase.

nodes.name: Operators on several qubits
nodes.definition: A ⊗ B acts on a pair; a Pauli string such as X⊗Z⊗I acts letter by letter.

nodes.name: Bell states
nodes.definition: The four maximally entangled two-qubit states, e.g. (|00⟩ + |11⟩)/√2.

nodes.name: Stabilizers of a state
nodes.definition: An operator that leaves a state exactly unchanged; XX and ZZ both fix (|00⟩ + |11⟩)/√2.

nodes.name: GHZ states
nodes.definition: (|0…0⟩ + |1…1⟩)/√2: all qubits agree in Z, and the product of X on every qubit is +1.

nodes.name: Commuting Pauli products
nodes.definition: Products of Pauli matrices that commute can all have definite values at once.

nodes.name: Teleportation
nodes.definition: A shared Bell pair, a Bell measurement and a Pauli fix-up chosen by the outcomes move a qubit state.

nodes.name: Mixed states
nodes.definition: A probabilistic mixture of states, described by a density matrix.

nodes.name: Noise channels
nodes.definition: The general way an open system changes a state, written with Kraus operators.

nodes.name: Depolarizing noise
nodes.definition: With probability p a qubit suffers a random Pauli error; the Bloch ball shrinks.

nodes.name: No cloning
nodes.definition: No machine copies an unknown quantum state, so plain backup copies are impossible.

nodes.name: Probability
nodes.definition: Chances over a list of outcomes that add to one.

nodes.name: The binomial distribution
nodes.definition: The chance of exactly w successes in N independent tries of chance q is C(N,w) q^w (1 − q)^{N−w}.

nodes.name: XOR
nodes.definition: Adding bits without carrying: 1 ⊕ 1 = 0.

nodes.name: Linear algebra over bits
nodes.definition: Row reduction, rank, kernel and check matrices with arithmetic mod 2; a check matrix turns an error into a syndrome.

nodes.name: Counting cost
nodes.definition: Polynomial versus exponential growth of resources with problem size.

nodes.name: Clock arithmetic
nodes.definition: Counting mod ℓ: positions wrap around, as on a clock face or a torus.

nodes.name: Period finding
nodes.definition: The quantum step of factoring, the classic motivating application.

nodes.name: Hamiltonians generate evolution
nodes.definition: Waiting a time t applies e^{−iHt}, built from the Hamiltonian H.

nodes.name: Why protecting qubits is hard
nodes.definition: Errors are continuous, copies are forbidden and looking disturbs the state, yet redundancy is still possible through entanglement.

nodes.name: Bit-flip and phase-flip codes
nodes.definition: Spread one qubit over three; the parities Z₁Z₂ and Z₂Z₃ locate a flip without reading the data.

nodes.name: Logical qubits
nodes.definition: A qubit stored in a protected subspace of many physical qubits.

nodes.name: Syndromes
nodes.definition: The pattern of check outcomes an error causes; it names the error without revealing the data.

nodes.name: Discrete errors suffice
nodes.definition: Correcting X, Z (and so Y) on a qubit corrects every error on it.

nodes.name: The Shor code
nodes.definition: Nine qubits protecting one against any single-qubit error: a phase-flip code of bit-flip codes.

nodes.name: Error-correction conditions
nodes.definition: A code corrects a set of errors exactly when those errors cannot tell code states apart (Knill–Laflamme).

nodes.name: Classical linear codes
nodes.definition: Codewords form the kernel of a check matrix; distance is the lightest non-zero codeword; every code has a dual.

nodes.name: [[n, k, d]] notation
nodes.definition: n physical qubits, k logical qubits, distance d; such a code corrects any ⌊(d − 1)/2⌋ errors.

nodes.name: CSS codes
nodes.definition: X-type checks from one classical code and Z-type checks from another; they commute when the two check matrices are orthogonal.

nodes.name: The Steane code
nodes.definition: The [[7,1,3]] CSS code built from the Hamming code.

nodes.name: The Pauli group
nodes.definition: Strings of I, X, Y, Z on n qubits with phases ±1, ±i; any two strings either commute or anticommute.

nodes.name: Paulis as bit vectors
nodes.definition: Up to phase a Pauli string is a pair of bit vectors (x|z); two strings anticommute when the symplectic product is 1.

nodes.name: Stabilizer groups and codes
nodes.definition: A commuting group of Pauli strings without −I; the code is the space all of them fix.

nodes.name: Generators and the check matrix
nodes.definition: Independent generators are rows of a binary matrix; n qubits and r independent generators leave k = n − r logical qubits.

nodes.name: Logical operators
nodes.definition: Pauli strings that commute with every stabilizer but are not stabilizers; they act on the stored qubits.

nodes.name: Code distance
nodes.definition: The weight of the lightest logical operator: the fewest qubit errors that can change the stored data unseen.

nodes.name: CSS codes as stabilizer codes
nodes.definition: A CSS code has X-type and Z-type generators; all logical qubits can be prepared in |0⟩ or |+⟩ and read out qubit by qubit.

nodes.name: The Clifford group
nodes.definition: Unitaries that map Pauli strings to Pauli strings under conjugation; generated by H, S and CNOT.

nodes.name: Measuring a Pauli on a stabilizer state
nodes.definition: A commuting Pauli gives a fixed outcome; an anticommuting one gives a coin flip and replaces one generator.

nodes.name: Gottesman–Knill
nodes.definition: Circuits of Clifford gates and Pauli measurements on stabilizer states can be simulated efficiently by a classical computer.

nodes.name: Measuring a check with an ancilla
nodes.definition: Prepare one ancilla in |+⟩, apply controlled-Paulis to the check's qubits, read the ancilla in X.

nodes.name: Why fault tolerance
nodes.definition: Useful algorithms need billions of operations, so logical errors must be pushed far below what any physical part achieves.

nodes.name: Tanner graphs
nodes.definition: A two-coloured graph with one node per qubit and per check, joined when the check acts on the qubit.

nodes.name: The toric code
nodes.definition: Qubits on the edges of a grid on a torus, X checks on vertices and Z checks on faces, each of weight 4.

nodes.name: Logicals as loops
nodes.definition: On the torus the logical operators are strings that wrap around; two independent directions give two logical qubits.

nodes.name: The planar surface code
nodes.definition: Cutting the torus open with two kinds of boundary leaves one logical qubit, whose operators run boundary to boundary.

nodes.name: The rotated surface code
nodes.definition: The compact layout with d² data and d² − 1 check qubits, about 2d² in all, for distance d.

nodes.name: Surface-code patches
nodes.definition: One logical qubit stored as a rotated surface-code tile; the unit of surface-code architectures and magic-state factories.

nodes.name: Syndrome cycles
nodes.definition: One round that measures every check through its check qubit, with the gates ordered so that checks do not disturb each other.

nodes.name: Circuit-level noise
nodes.definition: Every preparation, gate, idle and measurement can fail with probability of order p.

nodes.name: Phenomenological noise
nodes.definition: A simpler model with only data-qubit errors and flipped check outcomes between perfect rounds.

nodes.name: Detectors in space-time
nodes.definition: The parity of a check in two consecutive rounds; a change marks an error event at a point in space and time.

nodes.name: Decoders
nodes.definition: An algorithm that turns detector events into a correction; it fails when error and correction together form a logical operator.

nodes.name: Matching decoders
nodes.definition: For surface codes, pair up detection events by the lightest connecting chains (minimum-weight perfect matching).

nodes.name: Pauli frames
nodes.definition: Corrections and measurement fix-ups are Paulis, so they can be tracked in software instead of applied.

nodes.name: Circuit distance
nodes.definition: The fewest circuit faults that leave no trace in the detectors yet change the logical result; at most the code distance.

nodes.name: Fault tolerance
nodes.definition: Gadgets built so that a few faults cause only a few correctable errors; the threshold theorem follows.
nodes.alt_home: Q19/Q20 if N&C §10.6 is pulled in

nodes.name: Thresholds
nodes.definition: Below a critical physical error rate, making the code larger suppresses logical errors exponentially.
nodes.alt_home: Q19/Q20 if N&C §10.6.4 is pulled in

nodes.name: Logical error rate vs distance
nodes.definition: Per cycle, the logical error rate falls like (p/p_th) raised to about d/2.

nodes.name: Surface-code memory
nodes.definition: Repeating syndrome cycles and decoding keeps a logical qubit alive; its cost is about 2d² qubits per logical qubit.

nodes.name: Quantum LDPC codes
nodes.definition: Every check touches a few qubits and every qubit a few checks, however large the code.

nodes.name: Code rate
nodes.definition: k/n, the fraction of qubits that carry data; the surface code's rate falls like 1/(2d²).

nodes.name: The Bravyi–Poulin–Terhal bound
nodes.definition: Codes with local checks in a plane obey kd² ≤ const·n, so high rate and distance need longer connections.

nodes.name: Long-range connectivity
nodes.definition: Couplers that reach beyond nearest neighbours, e.g. two planar layers, allow codes beyond the bound.

nodes.name: Polynomials on a torus
nodes.definition: Sums of monomials xⁱyʲ with 0/1 coefficients and x^ℓ = y^m = 1: shift patterns on an ℓ × m torus; the transpose inverts exponents.

nodes.name: Bivariate bicycle codes
nodes.definition: Two polynomials A and B give X checks [A|B] and Z checks [Bᵀ|Aᵀ], which commute because AB = BA.

nodes.name: Counting logical qubits of a BB code
nodes.definition: k = n − rank H_X − rank H_Z, which equals twice the dimension shared by the kernels of A and B.

nodes.name: BB codes as a toric code with long edges
nodes.definition: Unit cells of two qubits and two checks on a torus: short edges give the toric code, two long edges per check give the rest.

nodes.name: The gross and two-gross codes
nodes.definition: The [[144,12,12]] and [[288,12,18]] BB codes: 12 logical qubits in 288 or 576 physical qubits including check qubits.

nodes.name: The BB syndrome cycle
nodes.definition: A depth-8 cycle measures every check of a BB code; C cycles take 8C + 1 steps.

nodes.name: Automorphisms as logical gates
nodes.definition: A permutation of qubits that maps the checks onto the checks performs a logical gate; for CSS codes it is a CNOT circuit.

nodes.name: Shift automorphisms
nodes.definition: Translating every qubit of a BB code across the torus maps the code to itself.

nodes.name: Belief propagation and OSD
nodes.definition: Messages on the Tanner graph estimate which qubits erred; degeneracy can stall them, and ordered-statistics post-processing finishes the job.

nodes.name: Relay-BP
nodes.definition: BP with disordered memory terms and a relay of reruns: accurate enough for BB codes and small enough for real-time hardware.

nodes.name: Measuring a logical operator
nodes.definition: Learn the ±1 value of one logical Pauli while disturbing nothing else stored.

nodes.name: Pauli product measurements
nodes.definition: Measure a product such as X̄⊗X̄ of two logical qubits without measuring either factor.

nodes.name: Code deformation
nodes.definition: Change the checks for a while; the stored data survive if the distance stays large throughout.

nodes.name: Lattice surgery
nodes.definition: Merge two surface-code patches along a seam for d rounds: the product of the new seam checks is the joint logical parity; then split.

nodes.name: Cycles of a graph
nodes.definition: A connected graph with V vertices and E edges has E − V + 1 independent cycles; a cycle basis lists them.

nodes.name: Gauging measurement
nodes.definition: Attach a graph whose vertices sit on the logical's support: new edge qubits start in |0⟩, vertex checks multiply to the logical, cycle checks keep the code consistent.

nodes.name: Expansion keeps the distance
nodes.definition: If every set of vertices has enough edges leaving it (Cheeger constant ≥ 1, or relative expansion), the deformed code keeps distance d.

nodes.name: Subsystem codes
nodes.definition: Codes with gauge operators that need not be fixed; the stabilizers are the gauge elements that commute with all others.

nodes.name: Space-like and time-like failures
nodes.definition: A measurement fails by corrupting the stored data or by flipping its own outcome; enough rounds (about d) guard the second.

nodes.name: Bridges
nodes.definition: Extra qubits and checks that join two measurement graphs so that a product of logicals is measured as one operation.

nodes.name: Adapters between codes
nodes.definition: A bridge built to join measurement graphs of different codes, keeping distance through relative expansion.

nodes.name: Clifford gates are not enough
nodes.definition: Because Clifford circuits are classically simulable, a quantum computer needs at least one more gate.

nodes.name: Clifford + T is universal
nodes.definition: Adding the T gate lets circuits approximate any unitary as closely as wanted.

nodes.name: T count
nodes.definition: The number of T gates in a circuit, the main cost of a fault-tolerant computation.

nodes.name: Pauli rotations
nodes.definition: P(φ) = exp(iφP/2) for a Pauli string P; a quarter turn is a Clifford gate, an eighth turn is T-like.

nodes.name: Controlled Paulis from rotations
nodes.definition: A Pauli controlled by another Pauli is three quarter-turn Pauli rotations.

nodes.name: Measurements absorb Clifford rotations
nodes.definition: After measuring R, a quarter-turn rotation about an anticommuting Q acts like a measurement, and vice versa.

nodes.name: Pauli-based computation
nodes.definition: Push every Clifford gate to the end, leaving only Pauli rotations and Pauli measurements; the final Clifford just relabels outcomes.

nodes.name: Magic states
nodes.definition: T|+⟩ and its Clifford images: states that, consumed by Clifford operations, give a non-Clifford gate.

nodes.name: T by state injection
nodes.definition: Measure P⊗Z between data and a magic state, then X on the magic state: a T-like rotation about P, up to a Clifford fix-up half the time.
nodes.alt_home: Q20 if N&C §10.6.2 is pulled in

nodes.name: Real-time feed-forward
nodes.definition: Later operations depend on earlier outcomes, so decoding and corrections must keep up with the machine.

nodes.name: 15-to-1 distillation
nodes.definition: Fifteen noisy magic states, checked with a 15-qubit code, give one with error about 35ε³.

nodes.name: Post-selection
nodes.definition: Discard a run whenever a check fires or the decoder is not confident (a small logical gap).

nodes.name: Expected attempts
nodes.definition: If each try is kept with chance s, the mean number of tries is 1/s.

nodes.name: Magic-state cultivation
nodes.definition: Inject a T state into a small colour code, check it repeatedly with Clifford measurements, grow it and move it into a surface code, discarding failures.

nodes.name: T factories
nodes.definition: A dedicated block that outputs T states at a given rate, error rate and qubit cost.

nodes.name: Rotation synthesis
nodes.definition: Any z-rotation is approximated to accuracy ε by Clifford and about 3·log₂(1/ε) T gates.

nodes.name: Six criteria for an architecture
nodes.definition: Fault-tolerant, addressable, universal, adaptive, modular and efficient.

nodes.name: Fabrication yield
nodes.definition: The chance a chip has no bad junction falls exponentially with its size, which favours small modules.

nodes.name: Modules and components
nodes.definition: Code modules (code c plus LPU u), T-factory modules f, code–code adapters a and code–factory adapters a′.

nodes.name: The pivot qubit
nodes.definition: Logical qubit 1 of each module, kept free as the ancilla through which everything else is done.

nodes.name: ZX-duality of BB codes
nodes.definition: X(p, q) is logical exactly when Z(qᵀ, pᵀ) is, so X and Z logicals come in matched pairs.

nodes.name: The logical basis X̄₁, X̄₇, Z̄₁, Z̄₇
nodes.definition: Four weight-12 (gross) or weight-20 (two-gross) operators whose shifts give all 12 logical qubits, chosen to keep the LPU small.

nodes.name: Bell checks
nodes.definition: A check split over two check qubits that share a Bell pair; its value is the parity of their two X readouts.

nodes.name: Shift instructions
nodes.definition: Twelve hardware circuits move data through check qubits to shift the torus in 14 steps; together they reach all 36 logical shifts.

nodes.name: The logical processing unit
nodes.definition: A fixed ancilla graph (90 or 158 qubits) attached to a module that measures any Pauli in ⟨X̄₁, Z̄₁, X̄₇, Z̄₇⟩.

nodes.name: LPU measurement modes
nodes.definition: Half the LPU measures ⟨X̄₁, Z̄₇⟩ or ⟨X̄₇, Z̄₁⟩; the whole LPU, through its bridge, measures the other nine.

nodes.name: Scheduling by edge colouring
nodes.definition: Colour the edges of a bipartite graph so no two at a node share a colour; each colour is one time step of gates.

nodes.name: Scheduling the deformed code
nodes.definition: Ordering constraints keep parallel check measurement equivalent to sequential; colouring gives 12 steps per cycle, an integer program 9.

nodes.name: Bell couplers
nodes.definition: Hardware that makes a Bell pair between two modules in less than one syndrome cycle.

nodes.name: Inter-module measurements
nodes.definition: Bridges of neighbouring LPUs joined by Bell checks measure 36 two-module Pauli products.

nodes.name: Code–factory adapter
nodes.definition: Couplers wire a path of LPU vertex checks to the Z̄ of a surface-code factory, so any ⟨X̄₁, Z̄₁, X̄₇, Z̄₇⟩ ⊗ Z̄_T can be measured.

nodes.name: The T-injection instruction
nodes.definition: Make T|+⟩ in a factory, measure Z̄_T ⊗ P̄ with the pivot, read the factory in X; error and time add up.

nodes.name: Bicycle instructions
nodes.definition: The instruction set: 12 shifts, 15 in-module and 36 inter-module measurements, 6 T injections, plus the idle.

nodes.name: Failure spectrum
nodes.definition: The fraction f(w) of w-fault sets that defeat the decoder; a binomial sum turns it into a logical error rate at any p.

nodes.name: Counting low-weight logicals
nodes.definition: Two codes of equal distance differ in error rate by how many lightest logical operators they have.

nodes.name: Benchmarking instructions
nodes.definition: Each instruction gets a duration in time steps and a logical error rate per use under circuit noise.

nodes.name: Measurement-projection diagrams
nodes.definition: A circuit notation in which Pauli fix-ups after measurements are implied rather than drawn.

nodes.name: Spreading a Pauli over modules
nodes.definition: A GHZ state of pivots, made by ZZ measurements of neighbours, lets each module apply its own factor of a long Pauli.

nodes.name: Native measurements and rotations
nodes.definition: Shifts of the 15 LPU measurements give 540 cheap measurements; quarter turns built from them generate the 11-qubit Clifford group.

nodes.name: Synthesizing any in-module measurement
nodes.definition: Conjugate a native measurement by a few native rotations; it costs about 18.5 bicycle measurements on average.

nodes.name: Small angles on the pivot
nodes.definition: A Ross–Selinger word becomes a chain of T injections whose bases adapt to earlier outcomes.

nodes.name: The resource model
nodes.definition: q = M(c + u + a) − a + a′ + f physical qubits for n = 11M data qubits; failure ≈ Σ (count × error rate) over instructions.

nodes.name: Logical capability
nodes.definition: The longest random π/4-rotation circuit that still succeeds with chance ≥ 2/3 on a given machine.

nodes.name: The surface-code baseline
nodes.definition: Patches of 2d² qubits, half for routing, per-cycle error 0.03(p/0.01)^{d/2}, each rotation d cycles plus a factory wait.

nodes.name: Product formulas
nodes.definition: Split e^{−iHt} into short alternating steps of the Hamiltonian's commuting parts; fourth order keeps errors small.

nodes.name: The TFIM benchmark
nodes.definition: A 10 × 10 transverse-field Ising evolution compiled to 184 000 small Pauli rotations.

nodes.name: Larger BB codes
nodes.definition: A conjectured family with the same A and B on bigger tori, whose kd²/n approaches 24 against 1 for the surface code.
